findings.disposition: valid -- §2.2 states that the fresh path never sets the key and that an absent cached means false, is not a §2.1 failure, and is not recorded as a value the response carried.

greptile_round_6.note: Round 6 found the same class of defect five times: a rule written against one code path while the gateway has two. The 'no top-level reason' rule was true of a completed brief and false of a call-level refusal; 'no etag is not degraded' was true about failure and false as a licence to work; 'fails closed means nothing was retained' was true of two local refusals and false of a timeout over two planes; 'the catalogue routes on kind' was true of the catalogue and false of the gateway that writes to it. Each fix is now scoped to the path it is true of, and verify.sh asserts both the new rule and the absence of the wording it replaced. The receipt's own approval was the fifth instance: a stamp true of one tip, read by the gate as true of any.

findings.title: Turn ack fails G-6
findings.disposition: valid -- turn acks moved out of approvals[] into loop_acks (new SS3.1). Of the two remedies offered, completing the fields is actively unsafe: G-6 pairs approvals to destructive ops by COUNT, so a four-field turn ack makes an unrelated rm -rf report as approved. Both directions reproduced and recorded; approvals[] is now documented as g5/g6 only.

findings.title: Approval cannot be stamped
findings.disposition: valid -- documented, not faked. The preflight gates the pre-stamp receipt and G-2 fails an absent approved_by unconditionally, so the tool deadlocks on its own input. SS4 now records the deadlock, the reviewed-commit route that works today (with the sha in the note), and that no placeholder may be written. The one-line fix is bot-01's or bot-06's and is in blockers with the patch. approved_by stays unset.

findings.title: Negative test cannot run
findings.disposition: valid -- and the && was the worse half. Both negative tests are re-recorded as three commands each (mutate / check / restore) so the exit code belongs to the check, with the python3 -c written out in full and an assert on its own anchor so a stale anchor fails loudly instead of no-opping into a false pass. Re-run at this tip; the round-7 test follows the same shape.

findings.title: Loop checks not enforced in PR workflow
findings.disposition: valid, NOT fixed -- every CI path is foreign to bot-00 (.github/workflows/** and ci/.github/workflows/** are bot-05's; ci/.github/** and ci/gates/** are bot-06's). The two steps are now written out verbatim in the verify.sh header with their requirements (no args, no credentials, no network), and verify.sh asserts that nothing in the skill, the docs or the script claims CI runs them.

greptile_round_7.note: Round 7 moved up a level: rounds 1-6 were about rules that were true of one code path and false of another, and round 7 is about rules that were consistent but collided with a gate. The turn ack was correct as prose and wrong as a receipt field; the unstamped receipt was correct as a state and unreachable as a workflow; the negative test was correct as an idea and unrunnable as a command. In all three the earlier round's fix created the defect -- round 6 cleared approved_by without checking that anything could set it again, and wrote the negative tests as prose-shaped abbreviations rather than commands. The lesson recorded for round 8: a rule about a receipt field is a claim about the gates that read it, and belongs checked against them.

findings.title: Approval advances the reviewed tip
findings.disposition: valid, and the root cause is structural. A stamp delivered as a commit cannot describe the head it is committed to, so the tip chase was inevitable rather than unlucky. New rule: an approval must be bound to a sha and must not create one. Broken workaround removed from both files (asserted absent); mechanism specified as a check run on the reviewed sha, with the receipt carrying approval_ref rather than a stamp.

findings.title: G-6 fixtures not in repo
findings.disposition: valid -- fixtures committed under the loop skill's fixtures/ with a README, and verify.sh now EXECUTES both and asserts their exit codes, so the false-PASS reasoning is machine-checked rather than prose.

findings.title: Negative test can wipe local edits
findings.disposition: valid -- verify.sh takes a DESK_LOOP_ROOT override and the negative tests moved into fixtures/negative-tests.sh, which mutates a git archive scratch copy with the working-tree files overlaid and never writes to the tree. Proven by running it with 205 lines of uncommitted edits present.

findings.title: desk_receipt_approve preflight deadlock
findings.disposition: NOT FIXED -- foreign paths, and the work order conflicts with its own DoD. services/** is bot-01's and ci/gates/** is bot-06's; editing either fails G-1, which the order requires to exit 0. Both patches specified in blockers and the conflict raised to the dispatcher. Round 8 also demotes it: repairing the preflight makes the tool work but still commits the stamp, which restarts the tip chase.

findings.title: loop_acks not in shared contract
findings.disposition: valid -- six-field contract table added, with why no gate reads it, the human check that applies today, and the exact G-2 rule for bot-06 plus the warning that it must not go in check_rollback.py. The contract file itself is bot-06's; the ask is in blockers.

findings.title: Claim cites wrong evidence index
findings.disposition: valid -- the claim asserted three things (verify.sh green, templates byte-identical, G-1/G-3 clean) and cited one command. evidence_command_index is a single int, so it is split into four claims each citing its own command.

findings.title: V_SELF tautology
findings.disposition: valid -- the assertion searched the whole file for a literal that the assertion itself contains, so it passed regardless of the comment it protected. The honesty checks now search V_HEAD, the comment block above `set -euo pipefail`, which holds no assertion text.

greptile_round_8.note: Round 8's P1-1 is the first finding in eight rounds that invalidated a MECHANISM rather than a sentence, and it did so by pointing at something the previous seven rounds had all demonstrated without noticing: every fix push moved the head past the reviewed tip. The receipt recorded each one and never drew the conclusion. The other three findings are the same class as round 7's -- evidence that could not be re-run (a /tmp fixture, a restore step that destroys its own context) and an assertion that could not fail (the V_SELF tautology). Taken together the lesson for round 9: check the evidence the way the rules get checked. A negative test that cannot fail, a fixture that cannot be found and a claim citing the wrong command are all the same defect as a rule asserted against one code path -- something that looks like verification and is not.

findings.title: Human grantor can disappear
findings.disposition: valid -- one `granted_by` field let a build seat record a complete, gate-clean entry naming only a seat, which is a degraded turn with no human in it reading as compliance. Split into human_granted_by (required, a person, seat ids rejected) and relayed_by (the seat that carried the ask). Fail-closed table added, LEAD explicitly not exempt, and G-2 now enforces it -- see the cross-ownership commit.

findings.title: Approval cannot be stamped
findings.disposition: FIXED, by crossing ownership on instruction. receipt_approve now stamps into a candidate and gates the candidate, in the order the work order specified. Both sides reproduced against the real gate. services/** is bot-01's, so this is a deliberate G-1 violation isolated in commit 9b220cc. It does not close round 8's P1-1: the tool still commits the stamp and so advances the tip, which is why approved_by stays unset.

findings.title: Fixture lacks a valid destructive approval
findings.disposition: valid -- the fixture claimed to show a properly-approved destructive op rejected because of a turn ack, but its only approval WAS the turn ack, so the rm -rf was unapproved and the FAIL was partly legitimate. A real four-field approval is added; it now fails solely on approvals[1]. A third control fixture was added showing the corrected shape passing.

findings.title: Scratch overlays only the loop skill
findings.disposition: valid -- the generator, templates and check_rollback.py were tested at HEAD while the rules under test lived in the working tree. All inputs are now overlaid, and a new case parses every load() out of verify.sh and fails if one is not in OVERLAY, so the comment cannot go stale. It caught the three files this round added on its first run.

findings.title: files_changed stale at 15 paths
findings.disposition: valid -- regenerated from git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD rather than maintained by hand, which is how it drifted, with a note recording that it is now derived.

findings.title: loop_acks not in shared contract
findings.disposition: FIXED, by crossing ownership on instruction. The field is in skills/verification-receipts/SKILL.md beside approvals[] with the entry shape and the warning that check_rollback.py must never read it, and check_receipt.py enforces six required fields, the condition vocabulary and the seat-id rejection. greptile_round_9.note: Round 9 is the first where the fix required crossing a seat boundary, and the shape of that matters more than the code: LEAD raised the conflict between 'fix the tool' and 'G-1 exits 0' rather than resolving it silently, was told to proceed, and then made the crossing as small and as reversible as it could be -- three files, one commit, G-1 green on the LEAD-only commit beside it, and the violation recorded in claims, unverified and blockers rather than buried. The substantive lesson is the P1-1 one: for eight rounds the ack rules were prose, and prose could not stop a seat writing its own id into the grantor field. The rule only became real when a gate rejected it, which is the same thing this receipt has been saying about claims and commands since round 1.
